description: The cloud-init user-data baked into the QEMU/Nix image build (referenced by qemu-arm64-nix.pkr.hcl:96 as ssh_password = "ubuntu") assigns the crypt hash of the plaintext 'ubuntu' to both the root and ubuntu accounts, sets lock_passwd: false, and enables ssh_pwauth: True. No subsequent provisioner re-locks these accounts or disables password authentication before the image is captured. Any instance booted from this artifact on a network-reachable host can be logged into as root over SSH with a known password. This yields full control of the database, all tenant data, and a foothold for lateral movement.
reproduction: 1. Operator or CI launches the QEMU-built supabase/postgres image on a host with port 22 reachable
2. Attacker runs `ssh root@<ip>` and enters password 'ubuntu'
3. Attacker receives an interactive root shell
technical_details: The root cause is that build-time convenience credentials are baked into the shipped artifact: cloud-init sets a known password hash for root/ubuntu with lock_passwd: false and ssh_pwauth: True, and the Packer pipeline never revokes them in a cleanup step, so the captured image ships with remotely usable default root credentials.
title: Cloud image provisioned with default root password and SSH password auth
